## Pull request overview Adds new transformerless evaluation and certification components to support Issue #27 by introducing performance certificate structures/serialization and a shortlist recall evaluator with gating logic. **Changes:** - Introduces `PerformanceCertificate` / `PerformanceProfiler` with hardware metadata, operational metrics, CID verification, and CBOR (de)serialization. - Adds `ShortlistEvaluator` producing recall metrics and Gate H / Decision D5-related outputs plus CBOR roundtrip support. - Adds new unit tests covering metrics, gating behavior, and CBOR roundtrips for both features. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | crates/uor-r4-core/tests/shortlist_evaluator_test.rs | New tests validating recall metrics, Gate H/D5 behavior, and CBOR roundtrip for shortlist reports. | | crates/uor-r4-core/tests/performance_certificate_test.rs | New tests validating profiler metrics, threshold behavior, CID verification, and CBOR roundtrip for performance certificates. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/shortlist_evaluator.rs | New shortlist recall evaluator/report types with gating logic and CBOR serialization helpers. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/performance_certificate.rs | New performance certificate types, CID computation/verification, and CBOR serialization, plus a profiling helper. | | crates/uor-r4-core/src/transformerless/mod.rs | Exposes the new transformerless modules behind `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`. |

review_comments.body: `HardwareMetadata` is imported but never used in this test file, which will trigger an `unused_imports` warning (and typically fails CI when running clippy with `-D warnings`).

`compute_cid` hashes `serde_json` output and uses `unwrap_or_default()`, which silently turns serialization failures into hashing an empty payload. Elsewhere in transformerless certificates, the CID is computed over CBOR bytes (via `ciborium::into_writer`), which is also what `to_cbor_bytes()` emits. Using JSON here risks non-canonical / inconsistent CIDs and undermines determinism expectations.

`PerformanceProfiler::profile` hard-codes a 64-byte cache line size while also emitting `HardwareMetadata { cache_line_size_bytes }`. If the metadata default (or future inputs) diverge from 64, the certificate will contain self-inconsistent metadata vs. metric calculations.

`worst_routing_error` is computed using `min(scores_graph.len(), scores_teacher.len())`, so if the vectors differ in length the tail is silently ignored and the reported worst error can be too small (which can incorrectly pass Gate H). It’s safer to treat a length mismatch as a hard failure for this metric (or at least force the gate to fail).
